question: Could transitions between characters offer evidence about a preference that the semantic ensemble and corpus unigram familiarity miss? Learn only from the current training text and ordered labels.
signals: On the same 2685 fitting comparisons build separate character distributions for preferred and less-preferred items. Preserve case and spaces and use start/end and unknown symbols. Compare order-zero character evidence to an interpolated prefix context of up to four characters. Mix each context with the immediately shorter context using its observed distinct continuation count as smoothing mass, backed by the label-free add-one-half corpus base. Use mean character log probability ratio for each item and subtract the two item scores. Each distribution counts only the fitting pairs for its role.
calibration: Train three such labeled count banks on group-disjoint inner folds solely to obtain out-of-fold signed scores for all fitting pairs. Fit one zero-intercept logistic calibration per order on the matching scores and mirrored pairs, then fit one full count bank. Report four banks (eight class-conditional distributions) and two calibrated slopes separately. Unknown symbols must have finite probability and reversing the items must complement their probabilities.
selection: Use the previously elected four-member reference. On the 1318-row review panel choose keep or one of the two calibrated models at 25%, 50% or 100%. Prefer less new weight then the simpler order on ties. Freeze the choice before comparing on the separate 1309-row panel, which is used only for a nonzero winner. Require positive second-panel delta and at least +0.20 points pooled for a subsequent ordinary trial. Reused development panels do not demonstrate transfer.
budget: Six local fitting operations counting a count bank as one operation, or ten if each separate class distribution counts individually. No pretrained generative service or weights, no model API, course-designated validation, official test or H2.
